newsitem.title: LEBANON: Banks rise in active Beirut trade.
newsitem.headline: Banks rise in active Beirut trade.

text.p: Lebanese bank shares rose on Thursday amid active trade in which all but one of the shares listed on the Beirut Stock Exchange was traded.
Brokers said the market was on the rise.
"The market is reopening every day on the buying side. There is a general rise that reflects a surge in liquidity," broker Johnny Yacoub at Financial Funds Advisors said.
The LIBX bank index rose 1.42 percent to 122.89, the BLOM stock index fell 0.3 percent to 908.55 and the LISPI index fell 1.05 percent to 84.87.
Banque Audi rose to $19.5 from $19.125 and Banque Libanaise pour le Commerce rose to $14.375 from $14.25. Trading in a third bank, Bank of Beirut BOB.BY, is due to start on Friday.
Banque Audi has risen 30 percent since its shares began trading on January 20 at $15 and Banque Libanaise pour le Commerce has risen 27.7 percent since trading began at $11.25 on December 30, 1996.
Solidere A and B were unchanged at $10.25 and $10.75. Turnover fell to 49,943 shares from 83,205.
Ciments Blancs traded for the first time since May 23, 1996, falling to $5.5 from $6.1875 on turnover of 300 shares.
Ciments Libanais held steady at $1.25 as turnover jumped to 37,500 from 11,500. Eternit fell to $2.00 from $2.0312 amid strong demand and turnover of 24,350 shares from 28,460.
"The fact that Ciments Blancs shares fell is not so significant after such a long absence and with such a small turnover," Yacoub said.
"Ciments Libanais and Eternit have been going up lately, reflecting the general rise across the board in the market," he added.
There was no trade in tilemaker Uniceramic.
Total BSE turnover dropped to 109,831 shares from 152,578. Value was $1,047,981 against $1,443,613 on Wednesday.
